title: When the River Moved: Ten Years on the Sallow Plain

headings.text: When the River Moved: Ten Years on the Sallow Plain

key_sentences: In the spring of 2016, the Sallow River left the bed it had followed for more than a century.
Heavy rain in the hills sent a flood down the valley in just two days.
The water broke through a low bank near the village of Orrin and cut a new channel to the east.
Geologists later found that the old bank had been weakened by decades of gravel mining.
Within a week, the new channel was carrying almost all of the river's water.
The farmers on the plain lost about a third of their fields to the new channel.
Instead of rebuilding the old bank, they agreed to farm on both sides of the new river.
A small ferry now carries tractors across the water twice a day.
Ten years later, the soil near the new channel is among the richest in the region.
The village council plans to measure the banks every spring from now on.
